task.speaker: client
task.text:
Hi Kenji,

Although Option 1 remains my favorite of the three, I don’t believe the silhouette is final yet. Comparing the work with the concept board has helped me understand that the distinction I’m seeking may lie in the V’s overall stance rather than in additional movement within its right arm.

The right arm should still have a quiet identity of its own, but more curvature is not what will create it. In fact, I think we may have restrained it slightly too much. I’d like to see a purposeful rise rather than a flowing motion—a confident, controlled gesture that retains some character.

What continues to draw me toward the concept board is not the Roman flares on the left arm; I still do not want those. It is the V’s overall presence. The reference has slightly more vertical reach, giving it aspiration and elegance without making it feel slender or delicate.

The name provides useful context for why that proportion resonates. Veillvé was created by blending a word for wellness with the French word for elevated (élevé). The idea of wellness elevated is therefore embedded in the name rather than functioning as a mere tagline. A subtle vertical emphasis naturally supports that sense of elevation without turning into a literal or contrived symbol.

Could we explore that proportion while preserving the same timeless, confident geometry? My instinct is that stance and proportion, not extra right-arm curvature, will provide the added distinction.

The silhouette still needs to feel inevitable, authoritative, timeless, and entirely resolved. Once it does, the champagne metallic treatment can introduce elevation, light, refinement, and emotional richness; the silhouette itself should establish confidence.

We feel very close. For the next refinement, I’d focus on proportion rather than inventing a new right arm.
